protections: Extension gate on save: the basename is derived from storage.filename through secure_filename+lowercase_ext and tested with file_allowed/extension_allowed before any bytes are written; a rejection raises UploadNotAllowed (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:314-319, 253-277).

Policy resolution: per-set UPLOADED_X_ALLOW/UPLOADED_X_DENY from app config plus the set's extension presets, evaluated by exact membership tests (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:63-66, 87-88, 268-277; src/flask_uploads/extensions.py:67-98).

Source-name containment: secure_filename strips path separators and leading dots from storage.filename before the join (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:279-283; src/flask_uploads/extensions.py:101-127).
Serve-time containment: send_from_directory confines serving to the configured destination (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:365-373).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The name argument is documented as an app-controlled override that gives the caller complete control of the saved file (docs/explanation.rst:165-174) and the tests treat arbitrary names plus the trailing-dot form as features (tests/test_flask_reuploaded.py:239-269), while the advisory mentions only a case-folding shape, so lowercasing the override looks sufficient.

Case looks already handled because get_basename lowercases the extension (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:283; src/flask_uploads/extensions.py:109-127), so the config literals, the preset iterables and direct callers of the documented file_allowed/extension_allowed hooks are assumed to arrive in the same case.

The library has only ever judged the final dot-suffix (src/flask_uploads/extensions.py:101-106), and the docs say the extension is a helper while the app may need additional actions (docs/explanation.rst:51-54), so earlier dot-segments are the web server's problem.

The layering is documented: ALLOW adds extensions that are outside the set and DENY only removes extensions the set would otherwise grant (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:138-141; docs/configuration.rst:41-45), so ALLOW winning over DENY reads as intended rather than as a denylist bypass.

folder and name are documented as giving the app complete control of the saved files (docs/explanation.rst:161-174) and the advisories are about extension suffixes, not path containment, so the caller-supplied path is treated as trusted configuration.

masking: T2 is only observable at the override sink once T1 is closed: before a re-check exists, save() writes any override name regardless of case (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:318-325, 336), so a mixed-case DENY entry cannot be distinguished there; after a natural T1 fix re-runs the gate on the final basename, a value such as DENY=('php',) still misses because extension_allowed compares raw strings (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:276-277) and AllExcept compares raw items (src/flask_uploads/extensions.py:97-98).

conflicts.what: Closing the unchecked override name by sanitising or rejecting separators in name/folder collides with the documented implicit-folder form, which must keep working (name='someguy/photo_123.' splits at src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:312-313 and must still produce someguy/photo_123.jpg per tests/test_flask_reuploaded.py:263-269), and with the trailing-dot append at src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:322-323 that T1's own re-check has to evaluate after extension substitution.

fairness_risks: The implicit-folder form in name must keep working (docs/explanation.rst:169-170; tests/test_flask_reuploaded.py:263-269): a containment rule that refuses any '/' in name would refuse a documented legitimate input shape.

A name ending in '.' must keep the uploaded file's extension appended (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:322-323; tests/test_flask_reuploaded.py:247-261): validating extension(name) before that substitution rejects the documented form.

Extensionless uploads with extensions=('') must keep working (tests/test_flask_reuploaded.py:343-349; src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:316-318): a rule requiring a non-empty final extension breaks them.

UPLOADED_X_ALLOW is documented to admit extensions outside the set (docs/configuration.rst:41-43; src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:138-141): an unconditional 'DENY always wins' rule contradicts it unless DENY is scoped to set-union-ALLOW.

Legacy dotted names such as archive.tar.gz must keep working (src/flask_uploads/extensions.py:121-123; tests/test_flask_reuploaded.py:37-41 and :48): a T3 rule that requires every dot-segment to be in the final allowlist rejects legitimate archives.

Only the extension is lowercased, the stem keeps its case (src/flask_uploads/extensions.py:115-127; tests/test_flask_reuploaded.py:43-51): a T2 fix that lowercases the whole basename changes stored and returned names.

file_allowed and extension_allowed are documented, overridable hooks (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:253-277): changing their case semantics silently changes the decision for application subclasses.

design.why: All four judgements are reached through the single public entry point UploadSet.save and can be tested with a Flask app plus TestingFileStorage, yet each has a different reason to dismiss and a distinct fix site: T1 is the reported rename-after-the-check on the name override (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:318-325, 336), T2 is the shared comparison layer where case is only normalised on the filename side (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:266, 276-277; src/flask_uploads/extensions.py:97-98), T3 is the last-suffix-only shape of extension() (src/flask_uploads/extensions.py:101-106), and T5 is the never-sanitised folder/name path reaching the same write sink (src/flask_uploads/flask_uploads.py:312-313, 325-336). It spans both model profiles (T5 is a clean deepseek M4 with a documentation-backed dismissal; T2 and T3 are how-type/coupled-value traps) and avoids T4, whose natural fix would contradict the documented ALLOW semantics and so imports a fairness problem rather than difficulty.
